questions.q: What does Post Mass Additions do with a line that was merged into an existing asset?
options: It deletes the existing asset
It creates a cost adjustment increasing the existing asset's cost
It creates a brand-new, separate asset
It ignores the line entirely
questions.explain: A merged line becomes a cost adjustment on the existing asset rather than a new asset record.

questions.q: What queue status does a line carry after it has successfully posted?
options: NEW
ON HOLD
POSTED
DELETE
questions.explain: Once Post Mass Additions successfully processes a line, its status changes to POSTED and it becomes a real row in the asset tables.

questions.q: Which of these is a common reason a mass addition line fails to post?
options: The invoice was paid by check instead of ACH
A missing or invalid category, or a date falling in an already-closed period
The vendor name contains more than 20 characters
The asset's location flexfield is set to the default value
questions.explain: Missing/invalid categories and depreciation dates landing in closed periods are common reasons a line fails to post successfully.

questions.q: What happens to a line that fails to post?
options: It posts anyway with incomplete data
It is permanently deleted with no way to recover it
It returns to the review queue needing correction, rather than posting with bad data
It is automatically merged into a random existing asset
questions.explain: Oracle Fusion Assets forces a correction rather than allowing a line to post with bad or incomplete data.

questions.q: Why is posting described as the "real boundary" between a candidate and an asset?
options: Because posting is only a cosmetic status change with no real effect
Because posting is when the line actually gets an asset number and starts a depreciation schedule
Because posting happens before Create Mass Additions runs
Because posting only applies to tax books, not corporate books
questions.explain: Everything before posting is just information about a potential future asset; posting is the moment it becomes a real, depreciating asset record.
